title: JUDGE FAIRLY, FOR JUDGMENT BELONGS TO GOD

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: And I charged your judges at that time, "Hear the disputes between your people and judge fairly, whether the case is between two Israelites or between an Israelite and a foreigner residing among you. Do not show partiality in judging; hear both small and great alike. Do not be afraid of anyone, for judgment belongs to God. Bring me any case too hard for you, and I will hear it." - Deut 1:16-17 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses gave the judges a clear charge: judge fairly, show no partiality, treat great and small alike, and do not be afraid of anyone. The reason he gives is profound: "for judgment belongs to God." Human judges were not acting on their own authority; they were standing in for God, and so they had to judge as He judges — with perfect fairness, without favouritism, without fear of powerful people.

This tells us so much about God's own character. He is utterly impartial. He does not favour the rich over the poor, the powerful over the weak, the insider over the foreigner. Every person stands equal before Him, and He judges each one according to truth. As Scripture says, God shows no favouritism (Rom 2:11; Acts 10:34). The same standard of justice applies to all.

This is deeply comforting for the vulnerable and the overlooked. In a world where the powerful often escape justice and the weak are ignored, God sees clearly and judges rightly. No one is too small for His attention, and no one is too powerful to escape His justice. He is the fair Judge of all the earth.

It is also a call to reflect His character in our own dealings. We are to treat people fairly, refuse to show partiality, and not be swayed by wealth, status, or fear of others. James warns strongly against showing favouritism among God's people (Jas 2:1-4). And there is comfort in Moses' final words too: "Bring me any case too hard for you." When we face matters beyond our wisdom, we can bring them to God, the ultimate Judge, whose wisdom never fails and who in Christ has dealt with our own case perfectly and mercifully.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you treat all people fairly, regardless of their status or power?
2. How does God's perfect impartiality comfort or challenge you?
3. What difficult matter do you need to bring to God, the wise Judge?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Righteous God, You judge with perfect fairness and show no favouritism. Help me to reflect Your impartial justice, treating all people fairly, and to bring my hardest matters to You, the wise Judge who has dealt mercifully with me in Christ. Amen.
